front: How do you rename a field in the Data pane?
back: Select the field and press `F2`, or right-click it and choose `Rename`. Type the new name and press Enter.

front: Does renaming a field change the source data?
back: No. It changes only what appears in Tableau. The new name is saved with the workbook and when you export the data source.

front: How do you restore a field's original name?
back: Click the small circular arrow at the right of the edit box. For several fields at once, select them, right-click and choose `Reset Names`.

front: Rename vs. alias
back: Rename changes a field's name (Signup Date). An alias changes how a member is displayed (`PRM` shows as Premium). Neither changes the underlying data.

front: Alias
back: An alternate name for a member (value) of a dimension, so its label appears differently in the view.

front: Menu path to create aliases
back: In the Data pane, right-click a dimension and select `Aliases`. Type the new label next to each member. `Clear Aliases` sets members back to their original names.

front: For which fields can you create aliases?
back: Only members of discrete dimensions. Not continuous dimensions, dates or measures.

front: Why can you not alias a measure?
back: Tableau does not permit re-aliasing measures because it involves modifying data values themselves.

front: Can you create aliases on a published data source?
back: No. When using a published data source, you cannot create or edit aliases.

front: Can an alias merge two spellings of the same city?
back: No. An alias is a display label for one member. To merge members you need a group.

front: Menu path to assign a geographic role
back: In the Data pane, click the data type icon next to the field, select `Geographic Role`, then pick the role.

front: Which fields can get the Latitude and Longitude roles?
back: Only numeric fields.

front: What happens when you assign a geographic role?
back: The field's icon becomes a globe, and Tableau adds `Latitude (generated)` and `Longitude (generated)` to the measures. Adding the field to Detail on the Marks card creates a map view.

front: What does "unknown" mean in the corner of a map?
back: Tableau cannot match some values to locations. Click the indicator and choose `Edit Locations`, or use `Map > Edit Locations`.

front: What can you do in Edit Locations?
back: Add a Country or State field to remove ambiguity (Paris, France vs. Paris, Texas), match unrecognized values to known ones, or enter latitude and longitude yourself.

front: Where can you change a field's data type?
back: Click its data type icon in the Data Source page grid or in the Data pane, or right-click the field in a view and choose `Change Data Type`.

front: What data types does Tableau show by icon?
back: Text (string), date, date and time, number (whole or decimal), Boolean, and geographic values for fields with a geographic role.

front: Why should a postal code be a string, not a number?
back: A number loses the leading zero (`07106` becomes `7106`) and Tableau would offer to add the codes up. Make it a string, then give it the ZIP Code/Postcode role.

front: What happens to text in a field typed as a number?
back: Text is treated as Null.

front: When should you change data types if you use an extract?
back: Before you create the extract.

front: Menu path for default properties
back: Right-click a field in the Data pane and open `Default Properties`. It holds settings for aggregation, comments, number formatting, color, shape and totals, depending on the field type.

front: Which default properties apply to dimensions?
back: Color, Shape and Sort. Sort also controls how the field values are listed in a filter.

front: Which default properties apply to measures, numbers and dates?
back: Aggregation for measures, Number Format for numbers and Date Format for dates.

front: What does the Comment default property do?
back: It adds a note, shown in the field's tooltip in the Data pane. It works for any field.

front: Default property or formatting a pill: what is the difference?
back: A default property applies to every future view when you drag the field in. Formatting a single pill or view changes only that view.

front: Are default colour encodings shared across sheets?
back: Yes. Color encodings are shared across multiple worksheets that use the same data source.
